title: This Apple Analyst Has a Prescription for the Company's Woes
text:

https://www.barrons.com/articles/two-ideas-to-fix-apple-51547484015 This Apple Analyst Has a Prescription for the Company’s Woes By Jan. 14, 2019 11:42 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Choo Chin Nian Text size
Apple (AAPL) should put two items at the top of its to-do list, according to one bullish analyst: Cut iPhone prices in China and bolster the company’s service offerings through an acquisition.
That was the Monday take from Wedbush analyst Daniel Ives, who has an Outperform rating and a $200 price target on the stock. (Ives target is 11% higher than the Wall Street average of $180, according to Factset.)
Apple’s stock is down 32% over the last three months, thanks largely to management’s report of slumping iPhone sales in China. The iPhone weakness has sparked broader conversations about the company’s business . Ives, for his part, wants to see two things happen within the next nine months:
• Cut prices “aggressively” in China. (That’s already begun to happen, according to many reports.) Doing so, Ives wrote, could “pull forward what we estimate is roughly 15 million to 20 million iPhones that would otherwise sit idle waiting for the next release, or worst case, move to lower priced competition.” Newsletter Sign-up
Apple announced three new iPhones late last year, and the early reaction to them has disappointed investors and management. Last week, Barron’s noted that some observers have already begun to look toward the 2020 models as a possible source of fresh innovation that could drive demand—though some changes are expected this year, too.
”If the installed base declines in China, Apple will face an uphill battle in the region for years and thus speaks to challenges world-wide around this latest upgrade cycle,” Ives wrote.
• Contemplate a “significant” acquisition in content to broaden Apple’s service offerings, creating more opportunities to bring revenue into its “ecosystem.”
“The company is playing from behind the eight ball in this content arms race with Netflix (NFLX), Amazon.com (AMZN), Walt Disney (DIS), Hulu, and AT&T (T)/Time Warner all going after this next consumer frontier,” Ives wrote. “While acquisitions have not been in Apple’s core DNA, the clock has struck midnight for Cupertino in our opinion and building content organically is a slow and arduous path, which highlights the clear need for Apple to do larger, strategic M&A around content over the coming year.”
The notion of Apple widening the range of services it offers—and, perhaps, bundling them —has been around for some time. In addition to video and news, one idea that’s been raised is videogames, with Barron’s Tae Kim recently suggesting that Apple buy Nintendo (NTDOY):
Like Apple, Nintendo likes to make money. Both companies have similar attributes: mountains of cash, gushing profits, beloved brands, loyal customers, and sticky ecosystems of software and services.
Ives sees movie and television studios as more likely targets—companies including Lionsgate (LGF.A) and Viacom (VIAB). He puts videogame studios, Netflix, and Disney at the bottom of his potential acquisition list.
Apple stock is down 2% Monday morning, to $149.32 as major U.S. indexes dipped .
